findings.question: q-biology-human-anatomy-physiology-0013
findings.problem: This is a throwaway distractor rather than a plausible confusion between pancreatic outputs. Stored urine is not an endocrine output; a student can reject this pair by recognizing urine as a urinary-system product without knowing either pancreatic output. The style guide requires plausible, mistake-based distractors.
findings.fix: Replace it with a plausible pair of digestive and hormonal products, and update its note to explain the specific confusion.

findings.question: q-biology-human-anatomy-physiology-0014
findings.problem: This is a throwaway distractor: nervous-system cells are not a plausible descendant of an activated B cell. A student can reject it simply because the stem asks about immune cells. The note about information signals does not establish a realistic B-cell misconception, as required by the style guide.
findings.fix: Use memory B cells as a plausible distractor, with a note distinguishing remembering an antigen from producing large amounts of antibodies.
